A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulation and physical-robot evaluations, synthetic diagnostic experiments, loss ablations, memory measurements, and action-horizon sensitivity results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, synthetic reconstruction results, velocity-distribution analyses, and DDE step-size sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Equation 14 revises the stated DDE computation from fixed-state, malformed network arguments to symmetric evaluations at z_(t±epsilon) and t±epsilon. The architecture, composite loss, and single-step inference remain unchanged. This establishes a correction to the written method, without establishing an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions retain three Adroit tasks, 34 Meta-World tasks, and the same three physical-robot tasks. The added diagnostics extend the existing synthetic-signal and manipulation analyses without establishing additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds a direct comparison of OMP against standard MeanFlow and a Vanilla Multi-step policy in Figure 6. V2's synthetic diagnostic compared Flow Matching with MeanFlow without OMP. Comparator membership in the main simulation and physical-robot evaluations is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include reconstruction of a four-frequency signal using identical backbones and an FFT amplitude-ratio metric in Appendix C.2.1, plus the DDE epsilon sweep in Appendix E.2. Previously reported training budgets, demonstrations, evaluation procedures, and horizon configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands component and mechanism validation: Table 1 adds DDE loss ablations, Appendix C.2 adds spectral reconstruction and four-task velocity-distribution diagnostics, and Appendix E.2 tests finite-difference step sensitivity. V2's preliminary diagnostics and existing horizon sensitivity study are retained.

E5.justification: The three-seed protocol using seeds 0, 10, and 20 and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. Added ablation and sensitivity rows follow the existing practice; no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: The empirical record expands substantially while retained benchmark scores remain unchanged. New DDE ablation averages are 77.2%, 80.1%, and 76.4%; Table 6 reports 80.8% at epsilon 0.005 versus 75.3% at 0.0001. Figures 6–7 add reconstruction and velocity-distribution findings under additional diagnostic settings.

T1.justification: Equation 14 corrects the mathematical finite-difference approximation, changing its evaluation arguments rather than merely its notation. Appendix B's spectral-decay theorem, gradient analysis, and memory derivations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about directional alignment, memory-efficient DDE computation, and effective single-step robot control. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.2 replaces slow precision-motion examples with an explanation based on lower action-space dimensionality. New appendix discussion interprets OMP's residual spectral attenuation and velocity distributions, identifies epsilon sensitivity, and attributes physical-robot failures to camera occlusion and open-loop action chunks.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses the directional-normalization stabilizer epsilon_dir approximately 10^-6, the default DDE epsilon of 0.005, and use of a single depth camera. Existing hardware, Table 4 hyperparameters, and supplementary-code availability statements are retained; these disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: Research positioning and cited-work membership remain unchanged. Match Policy and Diffuse and Disperse receive bibliographic revisions while retaining the same cited identifiers, and CLAP receives updated publication information. These are metadata changes rather than additions of distinct research.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the spectral-bias and ablation discussions, reorganizes Appendix C into setup and additional-results subsections, and expands Appendix E. It also adds acknowledgments and publication-header information. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain stable.

P2.justification: V3 adds diagnostic Figures 6–7 and sensitivity Table 6, enlarges Table 1, and adjusts Figure 4's image layout. The original robot photograph figure is retained as Figure 8, while Tables 4–5 move. These are localized display additions and rearrangements.

improvement.justification: The expanded DDE ablations and epsilon sweep strengthen component validation and practical guidance, while the corrected Equation 14, numerical defaults, and failure discussion improve reproducibility and transparency. The gain is limited by overstatement in the new diagnostics: Appendix C.2.2 claims all four velocity distributions approach zero, but Figure 7's Adroit Door histogram does not visibly support that claim. Headline benchmark evidence and appendix proofs remain unchanged.
